sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In a trial of 1,137 adults with resected melanoma, the personalised mRNA vaccine intismeran combined with the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab cut the risk of cancer returning or death by 42% after two years. Additionally, 82% of patients receiving the combined treatment remained alive and recurrence-free, compared with 70% taking immunotherapy alone.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It is the first individualised cancer vaccine to show positive phase III trial results. The vaccine targets up to 34 unique genetic mutations from a patient's tumour to train the immune system to prevent cancer returning.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Results will be presented at a Madrid conference and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Manufacturers MSD and Moderna are seeking regulatory approval and testing the vaccine against lung, bladder and kidney cancers.

sections.text: This summer's record-breaking heat and drought fuelled serious wildfires across the UK. articles.standfirst: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift.

gist: Enterprise AI success depends on the engineering system surrounding the model.
Workload constraints should dictate architecture rather than model capability alone.
Adaptable serving harnesses allow enterprises to absorb future technological advances.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Enterprise AI discussions have shifted from model capabilities to delivering intelligence reliably and economically at scale.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Serving architecture determines inference costs, memory utilization, and latency, directly impacting sustainable business value.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Organizations must measure dominant constraints and build adaptable systems to easily absorb future model and hardware changes.
